articles.title: A Day Longer Than a Year
paragraphs: On Venus, a single day lasts longer than a whole year. The planet spins so slowly that one turn takes about 243 Earth days, while one trip around the Sun takes only about 225. Venus also spins in the {{opposite|opposite}} direction from most planets, so the Sun rises in the west.

Its thick clouds trap heat, making the surface hot enough to melt lead. Because of these {{extreme|extreme}} conditions, only a few spacecraft have ever landed there, and none {{survived|survive}} for more than about two hours.

articles.title: Why We Remember Unfinished Tasks
paragraphs: In the 1920s, a story about restaurant waiters caught the attention of the psychologist Bluma Zeigarnik. The waiters could remember long orders, but only until the food was served. In her experiments, people tended to recall interrupted tasks better than finished ones, which seemed {{curious|curious}}.

This tendency became known as the Zeigarnik effect. Later studies have not always {{confirmed|confirm}} it, but the idea is still popular. Some students stop studying in the middle of a problem so their minds keep {{returning|return}} to it.
